title: GPT-6 Astra Autonomously Disproves Erdős Problem #1 (Distinct Subset Sums) in Lean 4
whyItMatters: Autonomously refutes Paul Erdős’s 1931 Problem #1 ("perhaps my first serious problem", $500 prize) in 27.1 hours for $405 with zero human steering, verified in Lean 4 + Comparator.
summary: As part of Epoch AI and Thomas F. Bloom’s FrontierMath Erdős evaluation (arXiv:2609.25050), GPT-6 Astra autonomously disproved Erdős Problem #1—posed in 1931 and famously called by Paul Erdős "perhaps my first serious problem"—in 27.1 working hours and $405 of compute with zero human steering. The proof was checked end-to-end in Lean 4 via Comparator and NanoDa (github.com/tadamcz/erdos1), alongside standardized $300-budget Lean 4 resolutions of Erdős Problems #74 (disproved) and #126 (proved) where four competing frontier models scored 0/68.
technicalHighlights: Autonomously disproved Paul Erdős’s iconic 1931 Problem #1 ($500 prize, 95 years open) with zero human steering in 27.1 working hours ($405).
Verified independently in Lean 4 using Comparator and NanoDa with zero sorrys (github.com/tadamcz/erdos1).
In the companion standardized FrontierMath Erdős benchmark (arXiv:2609.25050), GPT-6 Astra also solved Erdős #74 and #126 in Lean 4 while all other tested models scored 0/68.
caveats: Erdős #1 was resolved during extended-budget follow-up runs ($405 / 27.1 hrs) beyond the strict $300 standardized benchmark cap under which Astra solved #74 and #126; formal statement alignment was independently checked with Thomas Bloom.
